sections.h2: Where Fayette County deeds get recorded
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Fayette County Clerk's Land Records department, Room 132 at 162 East Main Street in Lexington. The phone number is 859-253-3344. The copy and inquiry counter stays open to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, yet recording ends at 4:00. A closing package that shows up at 4:15 sits until the next business day.

The clerk is a constitutional office, and its duties come from the Kentucky Revised Statutes. Besides recording, the office prepares property tax bills, runs elections and titles vehicles. Land records here go back to about 1792 and exist in books, on microfilm and as digital images.

For a seller, this office is where a sale ends. Once the deed is signed and the transfer tax is paid, recording puts the buyer's ownership on the public record. A closing agent normally walks the paperwork over, but the rules still matter when a deed is signed away from a title office.

Since January 1, 2020, Kentucky clerks have followed the Property Records Industry Association layout standards for real estate documents, and the Fayette desk enforces them. Nonconforming paper can be refused on the spot. Check the layout before anyone signs.

  • Paper: 20 lb white stock with no watermarks, 8.5 by 11 inches preferred and 8.5 by 14 accepted, printed on one side only.
  • Margins: keep the top 3 inches of page one empty for the recorder's stamp and leave 1 inch elsewhere.
  • Text: type no smaller than 10-point Times New Roman or similar, at most nine lines per inch, in black ink with dark blue signatures.
  • No staples or binding, no colored highlighter marks and no embossed seals unless inked.

The desk records far more than deeds. The list includes deeds, quitclaim deeds, easements, powers of attorney, land contracts, affidavits of descent or heirship, mortgages, releases, lis pendens notices, judgment and mechanic's liens, and wills. A corrective deed or an affidavit of heirship goes through the same desk.

sections.h2: How to get a deed to the clerk
sections.html:
Over the counter, the office records weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Three other routes work too.

  • E-recording: the office accepts submissions through CSC, ePN, Simplifile and Hopdox, the channels title companies already use.
  • Mail or courier: send documents by US Mail, UPS or FedEx to Fayette County Clerk, 162 E. Main Street, Room 132, Lexington, KY 40507.
  • Drop box: a box in the Helix Garage, near the second-floor entrance to the clerk's office and to the right of the yellow garage fee kiosk, accepts envelopes weekdays between 7:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. The last pickup is at 4:00 p.m., and documents must be sealed in envelopes.

When mailing a deed, enclose payment for the recording fee and the transfer tax, or phone ahead for the exact total. A package that arrives underpaid holds up the closing.

Kentucky law sets the base fee at $33 for a deed of up to five pages. KRS 64.012 carries the full schedule, and copy charges are the clerk's own. Request the current fee sheet from land records staff before closing day.

Typical charges at the Fayette County recording desk
Document or serviceCharge
Deed or release of mortgage, up to 5 pages$33.00
Each added page, deed or release$3.00
Each extra reference to the same instrument$4.00
Mortgage, up to 30 pages$63.00
Plat, per page, sized to 24 by 36 inches$40.00
Acknowledging a document$5.00
Copy of a record$0.50 per page, $1.00 per plat
Certified copy$5.00 for 3 pages, then $0.50 per page

Mail requests add $1.00 for postage and handling, and mailing a plat copy commonly costs $2.00. Copy requests by mail go on the clerk's form with payment, no more than two requests per form, and the office aims to fill them within three business days. The statute also lets the clerk collect a $10 reimbursement for permanent record storage on deeds, plats and mortgages. The window takes cash, credit cards or checks for copy fees.

sections.h2: Kentucky transfer tax on a Fayette sale
sections.html:
The seller, as grantor, owes it. The tax counts each $500 of declared value and rounds any partial block up. KRS 142.050 requires the county clerk to compute the tax and collect it before accepting the deed for recording. For a sale, value is the full price, liens included. For a gift, the clerk uses the estimated market price.

From each collection the clerk keeps 5 percent, then remits the rest each quarter to the county treasurer's general fund.

Transfers that escape the tax include divorce transfers between spouses, a parent or grandparent deeding to a child or grandchild for nominal consideration, foreclosure and deed-in-lieu transfers, delinquent tax sales, partitions, and deeds that only confirm or fix an earlier one. A clerk who records a taxable deed without collecting is fined $50 per offense.

sections.h2: Searching land records and protecting your title
sections.html:
The clerk's online portal is fayettedeeds.com. Land records from 1970 to the present can be searched, viewed and printed there, and many earlier records sit in the non-indexed documents section. All plats have been digitized. Since January 3, 2022, the clerk has indexed documents exactly as written on the document instead of using its older abbreviation list, so try a few spelling variations when you search.

A free Recording Notification Service from the clerk sends an email when a document is filed against a name or address you register. Each email address can hold 10 items. It is sometimes called a fraud alert. The clerk cautions that it gives no guarantee of catching every filing.

  • Check the portal now and then for anything recorded in your name or against your property.
  • Look often at vacant property to be sure no one is occupying it unlawfully.
  • Give the PVA and the sheriff your correct mailing address so tax bills and notices reach you.
  • If fraud is suspected, call the Lexington Police Department at 859-258-3600 and a lawyer. The clerk cannot remove a recorded document without a court order.

The same office collects delinquent real property taxes once the sheriff passes them on after April 15. Payment must be cash, a money order, or a cashier's or certified check, and delinquent bills can be searched on fayettedeeds.com. A house sold with unpaid taxes needs the balance cleared before a clean deed can pass, so get a payoff figure early. The County Attorney, at 859-254-4941, arranges payment plans.

sections.h2: Selling a Fayette County house with title problems
sections.html:
Lexington and Fayette County run as one consolidated government, so the clerk alone handles recording for the whole city. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,636 a month in housing costs, owners without one pay $599, and renters pay $1,164.

A house in poor repair or with a title tangle can still stall on the open market. A closing held up by a late-found lien or a missing heir's affidavit can go smoother with a cash buyer who takes the property as-is while the title issue gets cleared at the recording desk. A cash sale skips a lender's appraisal and repair demands, but the deed is still recorded the same way.

faqs.q: Which office takes a Fayette County deed for recording?
faqs.a: Record it with the Fayette County Clerk's Land Records department, Room 132 at 162 East Main Street in Lexington. You can walk it in, mail it, use the Helix Garage drop box or e-record through an approved vendor.

faqs.q: What time does the Fayette County Clerk stop recording documents?
faqs.a: Weekday recording ends at 4:00 p.m., though copy requests and questions are handled until 4:30 p.m. The drop box's last pickup is also 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies to a Fayette County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays $0.50 per $500 of value, and the clerk takes it before the deed goes on record.

faqs.q: Can I look up a Fayette County deed online?
faqs.a: Yes. Search fayettedeeds.com for land records from 1970 to the present, plus many older records in the non-indexed section. Plats are all online, and certified marriage records can be ordered there.

faqs.q: Does the Fayette County Clerk collect unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, once the sheriff transfers a delinquent bill after April 15. Pay the clerk the full amount in cash, by money order, or with a cashier's or certified check. The County Attorney, at 859-254-4941, arranges payment plans.
